clue.text: Why some cops arrive at demonstrations early

definitions.text: Why some cops arrive at demonstrations early

parts.words: Why some cops arrive at demonstrations early
parts.note: surface reading: police get to a protest ahead of time, the way anyone would to dodge a crush; setter's reading: heavy-handed police who hit protesters with batons, so their purpose in coming is to strike the assembled people

explanation.walkthrough: The everyday phrase for arriving early to avoid a mob is read literally: some police come to hit the protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means getting somewhere ahead of the masses, and literally names the motive of baton-swinging police.

clue.text: Fall behind after incorporating Virginia's hard work

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Falling behind after taking on Virginia's workload is a heavy labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort, a literary word for toil.

clue.text: Fruit ace mashed beneath helping of banana split

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath means the anagram is written below the first letter
a helping is a small portion, so only the first letter of the word is served

parts.note: first letter of banana

indicators.note: mashed fruit is pulped out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: mashed fruit beneath a helping of banana split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banana split' reads as the dessert, but 'split' alone is the definition. 'Helping of' banana is just its first letter, and the mashed fruit and ace go 'beneath' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bifurcate is to fork into two branches, which is a way to split.

clue.text: Visitor's heading to the basement, accepting spirit (mostly) and causing a strong reaction

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the moved word holds the trimmed spirit inside it
the head of the word, its first letter, goes down to the bottom, the last place

parts.note: a caller is a visitor; the 's reads as 'is'

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a genie is a spirit of Arabian folklore

explanation.surface: A guest heads downstairs to the basement and has a strong reaction to some spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading to the basement' means the head (first letter) of the visitor goes to the bottom of the word. 'Mostly' cuts the last letter off the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allergenic triggers an allergy, an immune response that can be severe.

clue.text: Gap underlying most of the economy

indicators.note: in a down clue underlying means this piece is written beneath the other
most of means all the word bar its last letter

parts.note: a rift is a gap or crack

explanation.surface: A shortfall that lies beneath most of the national economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of the' gives TH, and 'underlying' puts RIFT below it. 'Economy' looks like part of the surface's 'the economy', but it is the definition, in the sense of frugality.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy can mean careful saving of money and resources, which is thrift.

clue.text: One seat I arranged to occupy gently

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a single chair for themselves so they can sit down softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease into something is to settle into it slowly and carefully, taking up a place without force.

clue.text: Loudly deplore ingredient for sauce

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so the answer sounds like the word

parts.note: to rue is to regret or deplore

explanation.surface: Someone loudly complains about a component of a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The French cooking word ends in a silent X and is said like rue.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux is cooked flour and fat used as the thickening base for sauces such as béchamel.

clue.text: Catholic chief connecting Wisconsin to California's religion

parts.note: WI is the postal abbreviation for Wisconsin
the first letter of Catholic
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A senior Catholic figure links Wisconsin to Californian faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Chief here means the head of the word Catholic, its first letter, set between the two state abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is a modern pagan religion of witchcraft, founded in England in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Raised rackets about beginning of summit meeting

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up
about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: rackets are loud noises

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of summit

explanation.surface: Loud protests break out at the start of a summit meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit meeting' reads as one phrase; summit only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a period during which a body sits to do business, a formal meeting.

clue.text: Permissible to be decapitated? That's horrible!

indicators.note: losing the head means the opening letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: permissible means allowed by law

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that a beheading could be legally allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: LAWFUL without its first letter leaves AWFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful is an exclamatory synonym for dreadful, the reaction voiced by that's horrible.

clue.text: Unfinished alcove conceals distasteful assets

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one word sits within the other
something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a recess is an alcove in a wall
sour means unpleasant or distasteful

explanation.surface: A half-built niche hides possessions nobody wants to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: RECESS loses its last S to give RECES, which then holds SOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Resources are a stock of money or wealth an organisation can draw on, a synonym of assets.

clue.text: Song craft, if undisciplined, is something that needs to be controlled by professionals

definitions.text: something that needs to be controlled by professionals

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

indicators.note: undisciplined letters are unruly and out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A song about an unruly craft that only professionals can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song craft' reads as songwriting skill, but the song is AIR and 'undisciplined' rearranges CRAFT IF into TRAFFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement of aircraft is managed by air traffic controllers, trained professionals in control towers.

clue.text: Large amount of cash found at the source of Iraqi streambed

parts.note: a wad is a thick roll of banknotes

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of Iraqi

explanation.surface: A stash of money turns up at a dry riverbed in Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry valley or watercourse in Arabia and North Africa that fills only after rain.

clue.text: Religious New Wave rock band, into Weird Al

parts.note: Devo was an American new wave group

indicators.note: weird means odd, so the letters of into are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock band joining forces with the parody singer Weird Al Yankovic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird Al' reads as the singer's name, but Weird is the anagram signal on into, and Al stands unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotional describes worship or prayer, so it is an adjective close to pious or religious.

clue.text: Schubert works vocalized for governor

indicators.note: vocalized means spoken out, so the answer is what the word sounds like when said

parts.note: Schubert wrote hundreds of Lieder, German art songs

explanation.surface: Schubert's songs are performed aloud for a state's chief executive.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieder (German for songs) is pronounced like the English word for a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is a person in charge of a state or body, so a leader in the general sense.

clue.text: A.I., an inhabitant of Greece

parts.note: read as 'A, then I': the letter A followed by the letter I, with the word for followed by spelt out
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artificial intelligence is described as living in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation A.I. is read as a sequence of letters, A then I, and that phrase is spelt out in full before AN is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the Greek capital, so a native of that city is a Greek resident.

clue.text: I approach home seriously

parts.note: taken as written
to near is to approach
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone says that, without joking, they are getting close to home.
explanation.definitionFit: In earnest is an idiom meaning sincerely and with real intent, without joking.

clue.text: Words spoken by author White, perhaps, when in grave and imminent danger

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a grave is a tomb

parts.words: Words spoken by author White, perhaps
parts.note: E. B. White, author of Charlotte's Web, might introduce himself with 'I'm E.B.'

explanation.surface: An author describes being in a grave and pressing danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave and imminent danger' reads as one phrase, but grave is the container and only the last two words define.
explanation.definitionFit: A time bomb, literal or figurative, is a looming threat set to go off soon.

clue.text: Out-of-control outbreak: anger at Dad's misdirected drink

indicators.note: sent the wrong way, these letters end up out of their order

parts.note: a fit is a sudden outburst, as of temper or coughing
ire is anger
Pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A furious outburst at a father ends with a drink thrown the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' joins anger to Dad in the surface; the fodder is the three pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to whet the appetite.

clue.text: Recommended including tool in total

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to total is to add up
vise is the American spelling of vice, a clamping tool

explanation.surface: A suggested toolkit includes everything in one list.
explanation.definitionFit: Advised and recommended both describe a course of action suggested by someone giving counsel.

clue.text: Hewes returned money held by John Hancock, initially

indicators.note: held by means the reversed piece sits inside the initials
initially takes the first letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of John and Hancock

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the peso is the currency of Mexico and several other countries

explanation.surface: A founding father gives back money that John Hancock had been holding.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Hewes and John Hancock both signed the US Declaration of Independence, so the surface is apt. 'Hewes' is a surname, and the definition gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Hewes was a North Carolina signer of the Declaration of Independence, so his given name stands for him.

clue.text: To the Rev. Spooner, for example, mind a yokel

indicators.note: William Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the first letters of the two words change places

parts.note: say means for example and to mind is to heed, so the words give SAY HEED, which the Reverend's slip turns round

explanation.surface: A request to the famous Oxford don to name a country bumpkin, for example, and mind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the Rev. Spooner' means swap the opening sounds of SAY and HEED, which gives HAY SEED. A hayseed is American slang for a country bumpkin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayseed is an unsophisticated rural person, which is what yokel means.

clue.text: Magnificent politician, in coach, traveling north

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means reading upwards, from the bottom
in places one piece within another

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
Rep is short for Representative, a member of the US House

explanation.surface: A splendid politician takes a coach heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means of the highest quality, outstanding or splendid.

clue.text: Compete while internalizing bit of bad feeling

indicators.note: to internalize is to take something inside oneself

parts.note: to vie is to compete

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of bad

explanation.surface: A competitor bottles up a little resentment while playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibe is an informal word for an atmosphere or emotional sense given off, a kind of feeling.

clue.text: Drab loser's sung offering!

parts.note: surface reading: a dull also-ran's dreary attempt at a song; setter's reading: the song style of someone downcast and defeated, low feelings set to music

explanation.walkthrough: The music named for feeling down is what a gloomy loser would sing.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre is an African-American song form lamenting hard luck, loss and melancholy.

clue.text: Doctor I recall (yup) in a strange fashion

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient remembers, with a casual yes, that the doctor behaved oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the physician addressed in the surface; it is the verb meaning to tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiarly means oddly or unusually, which is acting in a strange manner.

clue.text: Get out and curtail fire

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, as a tail is docked, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: An order to leave, and to cut short the shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' could be the blaze to put out; here it is the verb for firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is an exclamation used to drive away an animal or person, telling them to leave.

clue.text: Shout wildly at European's extreme global position

indicators.note: doing something wildly means without control or order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged
a Pole is someone from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone yells wildly at a person from Europe who has gone to the ends of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Pole is the southernmost point on the earth, the planet's extreme end.

clue.text: Hint of excitement embraced by pleasant relative

indicators.note: to be embraced is to be held inside someone's arms

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: a hint is a tiny trace, here the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of excitement

explanation.surface: A kind family member hugs someone with a flicker of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member and so a relative.

clue.text: "70s Dance Music" float, behind schedule, has bits of mud splattered about in confusion

parts.note: disco is the dance music of the 1970s

indicators.note: splattered about means the following letters are flung around into a new order

parts.note: the bits are the separate letters of the word mud
to bob is to float on water
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A parade float playing seventies disco runs late with mud flung everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make '70s Dance Music' look like a song title, but it is simply DISCO; 'splattered about' then flings all the later letters into MBOBULATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Discombobulated is a jocular word for confused or thrown into disorder, so it describes someone in confusion.
